_auth_token_note: null means MINT one: the broker generates a token into webterm_token.json beside its state store and prints the URL to open. It never means no auth - a token is required on every connection, loopback included (#142). Set a string here to choose the value yourself (recommended across a fleet, so every host shares one password). Read it back with: python -m webterm.broker --print-token
_terminals_note: When false, this broker hosts no terminals: it refuses new launches (POST /launch, MCP launch_terminal, profile edits) with terminals_disabled, while sessions that already exist and agents reconnecting to /browserland are untouched. Use it on a hub (serve_ui true) that is only the front door to its nodes. serve_ui false makes this broker a node - no desktop page, reached over the API by another Browserland - and a node must host terminals, so serve_ui false with terminals false is refused at startup. GET /info reports both as role (hub or node) and terminals.
_peers_note: Absent by default. A peers object lets this broker relay an allowlisted set of another broker's routes under /peer/<id>/, so a browser or phone that can reach only this broker still reaches that one (its Hosts row set to 'from server'). Shape: {"b": {"origin": "http://<address>:4445", "mcp": false}} - an id of 1-64 of A-Za-z0-9_-, an http(s) origin with no path, query or userinfo, never this broker itself; mcp true also relays that broker's /mcp/* surface to agents holding ITS MCP token. Stores no credential. Needs the proxy extra (pip install -e ".[proxy]"), otherwise every /peer/* answers 503 proxy_unavailable. A bad peers value is refused at startup. See wiki/Technical-Reference.md, Peer proxy (#252).
_admin_token_note: Absent by default. Setting admin_token (a string of at least 16 printable ASCII characters, different from auth_token) turns on the admin credential class: mod install/uninstall/rescan, /mods/policy and /update/policy then also need it in the X-Webterm-Admin header, on top of the page token, and the desktop asks for it in an 'Admin token required' dialog (held in memory until the page reloads). Without the key the page token alone suffices and the broker logs one line saying so. Not the MCP admin token (that one is minted in Control Panel -> Access -> MCP access).
_restart_enabled_note: When true, this broker is allowed to restart itself (drain, then exit for its supervisor to relaunch) -- bouncing a broker that is hosting live sessions is deployment policy, not a login-implied right. Deliberately ABSENT here: with no restart_enabled key in this file, the decision belongs to the desktop's 'Allow this broker to update itself' row in the Update window (a human click, stored in a sidecar next to this file). Naming this key here at all -- true or false -- takes that decision away from the GUI and pins it to this file instead, which is the operator override for a hands-off deployment.
_restart_cooldown_seconds_note: Minimum seconds after boot before this broker accepts another authorized restart. Default 90: the supervisor's crash budget is 5 relaunches per 60s, so restarts at least 90s apart can never exhaust it. 0 disables the cooldown.
_update_apply_enabled_note: When true, this broker may download and apply an update to itself -- applying downloads and executes code as this process's user, so it is not a decision to leave lying around. Deliberately ABSENT here: with no update_apply_enabled key in this file, the decision belongs to the desktop's 'Allow this broker to update itself' row in the Update window (a human click, stored in a sidecar next to this file). Naming this key here at all -- true or false -- takes that decision away from the GUI and pins it to this file instead, which is the operator override for a hands-off deployment. Independent of update_check_enabled/the update mod's GUI toggle, which merely ask whether something newer exists.
